intro.lede: The layers of the system from the screen to the database, what each building block does and with which technologies, where it lives in the repository, and the paths a request takes.

l.clients.name: Clients
l.clients.summary: What the person touches: the web app, its offline mode, the mobile shells and the messaging channels.

l.edge.name: Edge
l.edge.summary: What stands between the Internet and the application: tunnel, content policy, rate limiting, sessions.

l.api.name: API and application core
l.api.summary: The FastAPI API split into business domains, its SSE stream, its ordered startup and its configuration.

l.agents.name: Agent orchestration
l.agents.summary: The LangGraph graph: routing, planning or ReAct loop, human approval, tools and response.

l.models.name: Models and costs
l.models.summary: Access to each provider's models, reasoning, structured outputs, embeddings, and the accounting of every call.

l.integrations.name: Integrations
l.integrations.summary: Clients for external services, open protocols, the sandbox and the voice channels.

l.background.name: Background jobs
l.background.summary: What runs without a request: single-leader scheduler, proactive engine, durable jobs, self-diagnostics.

l.data.name: Data
l.data.summary: Where state lives: PostgreSQL and pgvector, Redis, files, and the registers of what LIA did, read and decided.

l.observability.name: Observability
l.observability.summary: Measure, see, alert, review: metrics, dashboards, alerts, logs, traces.

l.delivery.name: Delivery
l.delivery.summary: How code becomes a service: images, continuous integration and its guards, qualified release, installer, demonstrator.

t.web.name: Web app
t.web.role: The interface: streaming chat, settings, dashboards and server-rendered public pages; all traffic to the API goes through the same origin.

t.pwa.name: PWA and offline
t.pwa.role: Installable, an offline page, web notifications; the cache follows the published version.

t.mobile.name: Mobile shells
t.mobile.role: One app per store, a client of a self-hosted server: the WebView loads your server's origin, and the native side only adds notifications, sharing and sign-in outside the WebView.

t.channels.name: Messaging channels
t.channels.role: Talk to LIA from Telegram and receive her messages; the bot's webhook is set by the scheduler leader alone.

t.edge.name: Tunnel, CSP and rate limiting
t.edge.role: Expose the service with no inbound port, set what the browser may load, bound each caller's rate, and read the caller's address in a single place.

t.bff.name: Sessions and authentication
t.bff.role: The browser never sees a token: a cookie session validated server-side, a second factor, a per-provider consent verified through a signed identity, and account emails (verification, activation, reset).

t.fastapi.name: FastAPI API by domain
t.fastapi.role: The business domains in DDD — routers, services, repositories — centralized exceptions, and a supervisor that doesn't load the application.

t.sse.name: SSE streaming
t.sse.role: The answer arrives word by word; steps, drafts and cost travel on the same stream; a streaming route holds no database session open.

t.startup.name: Ordered startup
t.startup.role: One module per subsystem and a single orchestration point; an incomplete registry refuses to start rather than die in silence.

t.config.name: Configuration and switches
t.config.role: Settings composed per domain, read from the environment; one switch per capability, read at the moment of the act.

t.i18n.name: Six languages
t.i18n.role: English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Chinese — in the interface as well as on the server, with no hard-coded strings.

t.langgraph.name: LangGraph graph
t.langgraph.role: The orchestration engine: a typed state truncated by tokens, saved at every step, which makes approval interrupts and their resumption possible.

t.router.name: Router
t.router.role: Classifies the request and, from a single embedding, scores the domains for the planner and ranks every tool for ReAct.

t.planner.name: Planner and executor
t.planner.role: A typed plan, mechanically repaired then validated, executed in parallel; a validation verdict is never presented as a failure.

t.react.name: ReAct loop
t.react.role: Setup, model call, tool execution, recovery, finalization; a single stop predicate; a turn that stops closes its own abandoned calls.

t.response.name: Response synthesis
t.response.role: Assembles the answer from the results and the declared contexts, states failures as they are, and declares the register that animates the face.

t.hitl.name: Approval and drafts
t.hitl.role: Classifies each sensitive action, presents the drafts one at a time, and draws the same card as a visual in the chat or as text on a ticket.

t.toolsys.name: Tools and manifests
t.toolsys.role: Each tool declares its bounded parameters, what it owes the person, and its domain; a gate records it in the effects register before it acts.

t.dataregistry.name: Data registry and context
t.dataregistry.role: Tool results become referenceable items: “the second one” points to a real object, not to a sentence.

t.promptsys.name: Versioned prompts
t.promptsys.role: Each prompt is a versioned file; each variable has a producer; the stable part comes before the variable part so that the cache gets used.

t.initiative.name: Initiative node
t.initiative.role: After an execution, decides whether to chain a follow-up action, with a catalogue limited to what it can actually execute.

t.llmfactory.name: Model factory
t.llmfactory.role: One native client per provider; the same cache boundary translated into each one's mechanism; a single seam between a reasoning intent and an API parameter.

t.reasoning.name: Reasoning
t.reasoning.role: A single stored shape for “think more or less”, a derived profile per model, and each coercion counted and logged.

t.catalogue.name: Model catalogue
t.catalogue.role: The truth about what each model can do and what it costs, with the provenance of each capability; managed through a workbook.

t.structured.name: Structured outputs
t.structured.role: Get a typed object from a model; an answer cut off by the token limit is a refusal, never a shorter document announced as a success.

t.embeddings.name: Embeddings and search
t.embeddings.role: Vectorize, retrieve by meaning and by words, merge under a semantic threshold; every input sent to the provider is an exact string.

t.pricing.name: Accounting and ceilings
t.pricing.role: Every paid call is bounded beforehand (account and instance), priced at the moment it is made, then recorded in the right ledger; each module declares where its spend is counted.

t.connclients.name: Connector clients
t.connclients.role: One client per provider, a single door to a category's active client; never an open database transaction during the network call.

t.mcp.name: MCP client
t.mcp.role: A pool of MCP clients per person, tool schemas read to the letter of the standard, tools gated just like the native ones.

t.skills.name: Skills and plugins
t.skills.role: Install, enable and run portable skills; a plugin brings skills and MCP servers in one go.

t.sandbox.name: Sandbox and egress proxy
t.sandbox.role: Run a script written by a model safely: network cut off except for one proxy, keys swapped in by the proxy, unknown hosts left to your decision.

t.browser.name: Automated browser
t.browser.role: Open a page, read it, browse it for sites that require a real browser; screenshots become the person's files.

t.voiceinfra.name: Voice: transcription and synthesis
t.voiceinfra.role: Transcribe and synthesize speech, with a model cache bounded per process and a voice modulated by mood.

t.live.name: Live transports
t.live.role: Each provider declares its connection mode and its way of delegating; the browser plays audio through a single AudioWorklet; no branching on a provider's name.

t.phone.name: Telephony
t.phone.role: Call the person or a third party, lend the voice read-only tools, and relay the conversation to the chat through a single closing step.

t.push.name: Push notifications
t.push.role: Reach a browser or a phone; on iOS, a relay carries only an opaque identifier and a contentless sentence.

t.scheduler.name: Single-leader scheduler
t.scheduler.role: A single process triggers the jobs; every periodic job carries a jitter so they don't all fire in the same second; recurrences go through a single engine.

t.proactive.name: Proactive engine
t.proactive.role: Selects, checks, generates and sends what LIA says on her own; each send is claimed before it goes out and settled from its result.

t.jobs.name: Durable jobs
t.jobs.role: Meetings, voice relays, projections: each long job is a claimed row, resumed after a stop, settled from an explicit result.

t.selfdiag.name: Self-diagnostics
t.selfdiag.role: LIA reads her own telemetry, gathers the evidence of an incident as it happens, and keeps a memory of it.

t.postgres.name: PostgreSQL and pgvector
t.postgres.role: The source of truth: accounts, conversations, graph checkpoints, vectors; migrations in a single chain, sessions that live no longer than their queries.

t.redis.name: Redis
t.redis.role: Caches, sessions, locks and claims; each key family declares its scope, and a purge removes only what its family declares.

t.storage.name: Files
t.storage.role: Attachments and files produced by LIA; each file says who produced it, and a reset removes only what it should.

t.registers.name: Traceable registers
t.registers.role: One row per action, per consultation and per turn; the instance can seal them into a per-account hash chain; exportable in full, never repaired.

t.metrics.name: Metrics
t.metrics.role: Every metric defined in the code is read by a panel, a rule or an alert — a metric nobody sees is forbidden.

t.dashboards.name: Dashboards
t.dashboards.role: Dashboards per subsystem, each query resolved to a real producer.

t.alerts.name: Alerts
t.alerts.role: Alerts that wake someone up for a reason, each with its runbook, validated as a matrix of configurations.

t.logs.name: Logs
t.logs.role: Structured logs with no personal data at INFO level, closed-set labels, read back through Loki.

t.tracing.name: Traces
t.tracing.role: Follow a request across the layers, and every model call with its tokens.

t.docker.name: Images and composition
t.docker.role: Production images pinned by version and digest, built from frozen installs.

t.cicd.name: Continuous integration and guards
t.cicd.role: CI orchestrates, the Taskfile implements: every step is a command a developer can run; thresholds only ever go up.

t.release.name: Release, deployment and installer
t.release.role: A tag builds a candidate, a disposable install qualifies it, then the release publishes it; the deployment reads its verdict from a file; an installer guides self-hosting.

t.demo.name: Demonstrator
t.demo.role: A public demo instance whose every protection is recomputed from the source of truth, and checked on every deployment.

tflow.request.name: The journey of a chat message
tflow.request.summary: From keyboard to screen, by way of the graph: one request, one stream, no token exposed.
steps: The browser sends the message to the API on its own origin.
The tunnel routes it; the caller's rate limit is checked.
The session cookie is validated server-side.
The chat route opens a stream and starts the graph.
The conversation state is reloaded from its checkpoint.
The request is classified, the tools scored.
A plan is written, validated, and executed in parallel.
Each tool goes through the authority gate and is recorded in the register.
The provider is called, with no database transaction open.
The answer is synthesized from the results.
It arrives word by word, with its cost, on the same stream.

tflow.llmcall.name: A model call, end to end
tflow.llmcall.summary: Bounded before, translated for the provider, priced at the moment it is made, traced after.
steps: The prompt is assembled: the stable part first, a single cache boundary.
Both ceilings — account and instance — are checked before any spending.
The reasoning intent is translated for this specific model.
The provider's native client sends the request.
An output cut off by the token limit becomes an explicit refusal.
Usage is read only once and priced at the time window of the call.
The parameters actually sent go into the call's record.
Tokens, latency and cost become metrics.

tflow.background.name: A proactive background job
tflow.background.summary: A single leader, a jitter, a claim, a send settled from its result.
steps: The leader triggers the sweep, offset by its jitter.
Eligible accounts are selected under every rule.
The sources are read, each in a short transaction.
The message is written within the spending ceilings.
The send is claimed before it goes out.
The notification goes out to the browser or the phone.
The effect is settled from the actual result of the send.

tflow.live.name: A Live session
tflow.live.summary: The browser talks directly to the provider; every request comes back to the graph.
steps: The person opens a Live session.
The API issues a single-use credential and renders the voice's mandate.
The browser opens the provider's transport (WebSocket or WebRTC).
A delegated request becomes an ordinary chat turn.
The graph runs it with its approvals and its registers.
The answer, bounded and flattened, is handed back to the voice.
At the end, a single closing step archives, tallies up and relays.

tflow.delivery.name: From commit to production
tflow.delivery.summary: Every guard runs before the push; nothing is published without qualification.
steps: The hook and CI run the same Task commands: lint, ratchets, tests.
On the tag, candidate images are built and tagged by digest.
A disposable install qualifies the candidate.
The release checks the evidence and publishes the version tags.
The pinned images are pulled onto the server.
The detached deployment writes its verdict to a file that is read back.
The demonstrator is redeployed and checked.

tflow.observe.name: See, alert, self-diagnose
tflow.observe.summary: Every signal has a reader; an alert has a runbook; LIA reads her own evidence.
steps: Processes publish their metrics, memory included.
Structured logs, free of personal data, go to Loki.
Grafana shows every subsystem.
An alert goes out with its runbook.
LIA gathers the evidence of the incident and diagnoses it.
